intelligence.human_view: He was looking at the page — the bottom bar and the rest of it — and he could see it: the colors at the bottom, the icons at the bottom, and the colors of the other ones on the page are not aligned. Some don't look as good, some are too neon, some are not the same. So we should have one set of colors — because if you just use the finest jewelry, the finest gems, the best of the best colors, the most elite parts and presentation, you don't need to do everything, you just use the best of the best: the nicest purple, the nicest gold, the nicest blue, the nicest reds, the most incredible rich teal greens and blues — the most beautiful colors there are, that exist in cars and jewels and design. And we have the official set, like nine, and they're aligned with the colors of the universe: 963 is the crown chakra, which is actually magenta; purple is actually 852 — he often refers to it as purple is the nine, because it goes into the nine, because there's a range from 852 to 963 where it becomes purple, and magenta is a kind of purple. What he's saying is: no whole bunch of different purples, no whole bunch of different greens, different blues. One set of colors that we use all the way through, with all our buttons. The search aligned with the purple on the icons — that's good, that's the example of right. But any unalignment shouldn't be there: there shouldn't be anything that's not aligned. One set of colors everywhere, none that look neon — all of them rich and valuable and elegant and jewel-like and real.
